newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on central bank support.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on central bank support.

text.p: The won closed firmer against the dollar on Friday after the central bank intervened repeatedly to halt the local unit's decline, traders said.
But the Bank of Korea denied it intervened, as it routinely does.
The won closed at 843.40 after opening at an intraday low of 845.00. It peaked at 840.40.
Traders said the bullish sentiment towards the dollar was quenched by the strong central bank intervention.
"The Bank of Korea sold about $300 million to slow the dollar's rise," said one local bank dealer.
Traders said the poor fundamentals towards the local currency haven't changed and the sentiment would remain weak for the near future.
"The dollar is set to rise unless the dollar/yen rate falls dramatically," said another dealer.
The won's base mid-rate is seen at 842.70 on Monday, compared with 844.60 on Friday, dealers said.
